meta.source: data/pre1_*.json から大問1だけを抽出した共通Q1データ

words.etymology: ギリシャ語 koimeterion「眠る場所」がラテン語・古フランス語を経て英語に入った。
words.example: The old cemetery on the hill has graves dating back two centuries.

words.etymology: ギリシャ語 diagramma。dia-「〜を通して」+ graphein「書く・描く」。
words.example: The teacher drew a diagram on the board to show how blood flows through the heart.

words.etymology: ラテン語 aequare「等しくする」(aequus「等しい」)から。
words.example: She solved the equation by isolating x on one side.

words.etymology: fore-「前もって」+ cast「投げる、見積もる」の複合語。
words.example: According to the forecast, it will rain all weekend.

words.meaning: 所有欲の強い、独占欲の強い
words.etymology: ラテン語 possidere「所有する」の派生語 possessivus から。
words.example: He became possessive about his girlfriend and didn't like her spending time with other friends.

words.etymology: ギリシャ語 horizon「境界を区切る(円)」+ -al。
words.example: Lay the board horizontal before you start cutting it.

words.etymology: ラテン語 redundare「あふれ出る」。red-「再び」+ undare「波立つ」(unda「波」)。
words.example: This sentence in your essay is redundant; you already said the same thing in the previous paragraph.

words.meaning: 徹底的な、思い切った、過激な
words.etymology: ギリシャ語 drastikos「効果的な、行動的な」(dran「行う」)から。
words.example: The company took drastic measures to cut costs, including laying off a third of its staff.

words.meaning: 引っ張る、(重い物を)運ぶ
words.etymology: 「引く」を意味する hale の異形。古フランス語 haler(ゲルマン語起源)経由。
words.example: The fishermen hauled the nets onto the deck.

words.etymology: ラテン語 invidia(invidere「悪意を持って見る」、in-+videre「見る」)から。
words.example: I envy people who can speak three languages fluently.

words.etymology: ラテン語 subtrahere「下に引く」。sub-「下に」+ trahere「引く」。
words.example: If you subtract 15 from 40, you get 25.

words.etymology: ラテン語 censere「評価する、判定する」。古代ローマの風紀監督官 censor に由来。
words.example: The government censored the film before allowing it to be shown in theaters.

words.meaning: 紹介、(専門医への)委託、照会
words.etymology: refer(ラテン語 referre、re-+ferre「運ぶ」)+ -al。
words.example: My doctor gave me a referral to see a specialist.

words.etymology: ラテン語 recipere「受け取る」(re-+capere「取る」)から。
words.example: She was the recipient of a scholarship for outstanding academic achievement.

words.etymology: bounce「跳ね返る」+ -er。「用心棒」の意味は20世紀に発達した。
words.example: The bouncer at the club checked everyone's ID before letting them in.

words.etymology: ラテン語 succedere「後に続く」(sub-+cedere「行く」)の派生語。
words.example: The CEO announced his successor before retiring.

words.etymology: trigger はオランダ語 trekker(trekken「引く」)から。
words.example: Loud noises can trigger a panic attack in some people.

words.meaning: でっち上げる(こと)、捏造する(こと)
words.etymology: ラテン語 fabricare「作る、組み立てる」(fabrica「工房」)から。
words.example: The witness admitted to fabricating parts of his story.

words.meaning: 保存する(こと)、節約する(こと)
words.etymology: ラテン語 conservare。com-「共に」+ servare「保つ」。
words.example: We're conserving water during the drought by taking shorter showers.

words.meaning: 放棄する(こと)、断念する(こと)
words.etymology: ラテン語 renuntiare「拒否を宣言する」。re-+nuntiare「知らせる」(nuntius「使者」)。
words.example: He renounced his claim to the family business.

words.etymology: 古フランス語 raençon。ラテン語 redemptio「買い戻し」と同語源(redemption と同根)。
words.example: The kidnappers demanded a large ransom for the hostage's release.

words.etymology: ラテン語 specimen「印、実例」(specere「見る」)から。
words.example: The biologist collected a specimen of the rare plant for study.

words.etymology: ラテン語 cavus「空洞の」+ -ity。
words.example: The dentist found a small cavity in one of my back teeth.

words.etymology: ラテン語 citare「呼び出す、動かす」(ciere「動かす・呼ぶ」の反復形)から。
words.example: The professor asked students to include a proper citation for every source they used.

words.etymology: ラテン語 distorquere「あちこちにねじる」。dis-+torquere「ねじる」。
words.example: The old mirror created a strange distortion of my reflection.

words.etymology: ラテン語 generosus「高貴な、寛大な」(genus「生まれ、家柄」)から。
words.example: Her generosity toward the local charity was widely admired.

words.etymology: ラテン語 turbulentus「騒然とした」(turba「群衆、騒動」)から。
words.example: The plane shook violently as it passed through an area of turbulence.

words.etymology: ラテン語 conicere「投げ合わせる、推論する」。com-+iacere「投げる」。
words.example: Without any real evidence, his theory is pure conjecture.

words.etymology: ラテン語 nutrire「養う」+ -itious。
words.example: A nutritious breakfast helps you concentrate better in the morning.

words.etymology: ラテン語 diversus「別々の方向を向いた」(divertere の過去分詞)から。
words.example: The city has a diverse population, with residents from over sixty countries.

words.etymology: 古フランス語 braine/baraigne。語源は未詳(ケルト語起源の可能性)。
words.example: Almost nothing grows in this barren stretch of desert.

words.meaning: 偶然の、たまたま一致した
words.etymology: coincide(ラテン語 co-+incidere「たまたま起こる」)+ -al。
words.example: It was purely coincidental that we were staying at the same hotel.

words.meaning: たるんだ、緩い、(商売などが)不振の
words.etymology: 古英語 slæc「緩い、怠惰な」。ゲルマン語起源。
words.example: Business has been slack since the new mall opened nearby.

words.etymology: ラテン語 sparsus(spargere「まき散らす」の過去分詞)から。
words.example: The population is quite sparse in this remote mountain region.

words.etymology: ラテン語 vastus「広大な、荒涼とした」。
words.example: The vast desert stretched as far as the eye could see.

words.etymology: ラテン語 vitalis(vita「生命」)から。
words.example: Clean water is vital for human health.

words.etymology: ラテン語 descendere「下る」(de-+scandere「登る」)の派生語。
words.example: She is a direct descendant of one of the town's founders.

words.etymology: ラテン語 triumphus。勝利した将軍の凱旋行進を指した。
words.example: Winning the championship was a great triumph for the team.

words.etymology: ラテン語 emittere「送り出す」(e-+mittere「送る」)から。
words.example: The new law aims to reduce carbon emissions from factories.

words.etymology: ラテン語 deficere「不足する、欠ける」(de-+facere「作る、する」)から。
words.example: A vitamin D deficiency can weaken your bones over time.

words.meaning: 繁栄する(こと)、生い茂る(こと)
words.etymology: ラテン語 florere「花咲く」(flos「花」)から。
words.example: The small bakery has been flourishing since it opened last year.

words.meaning: 誓う(こと)、約束する(こと)
words.etymology: 古フランス語 plege「保証、担保」。フランク語起源とされる。
words.example: Every member pledged to attend the meeting.

words.meaning: まき散らす(こと)、散らばる(こと)
words.etymology: 中英語期の語で、shatter との関連が指摘されるが語源ははっきりしない。
words.example: The wind sent leaves scattering across the yard.

words.meaning: うなだれる(こと)、しおれる(こと)
words.etymology: 古ノルド語 drupa「沈む、うなだれる」から。
words.example: The flowers were drooping in the summer heat.

words.etymology: ラテン語 reptilis「這う」(repere「這う」)から。
words.example: Snakes and lizards are both types of reptile.

words.etymology: フランス語(フランコプロヴァンス語 glacière 経由)、ラテン語 glacies「氷」から。
words.example: The glacier has retreated significantly over the past fifty years due to warming temperatures.

words.etymology: block に -ade を付けた語(barricade からの類推)。
words.example: The navy set up a blockade to prevent supplies from reaching the port.

words.meaning: 作品集、資産構成、書類ばさみ
words.etymology: イタリア語 portafoglio。portare「運ぶ」+ foglio「葉、紙」。
words.example: The artist showed her portfolio to several galleries before finding one willing to display her work.

words.etymology: ラテン語 abbreviare。ab-+brevis「短い」。
words.example: 'Doctor' is often abbreviated to 'Dr.' in writing.

words.etymology: ラテン語 attestari。ad-+testari「証言する」(testis「証人」)。
words.example: Several colleagues can attest to her honesty.

words.etymology: 古英語 ceorfan「切る」。ゲルマン語起源。
words.example: He carved a small wooden bird for his daughter.

words.etymology: 古英語 gieldan「支払う、報いる」。ゲルマン語起源。
words.example: The field yielded a record harvest this year.

words.etymology: ラテン語 radiare(radius「光線、車輪の輻」)から。
words.example: The stove radiated heat throughout the small cabin.

words.etymology: ラテン語 magnificare。magnus「大きい」+ facere「作る」。
words.example: The microscope can magnify a cell up to a thousand times its actual size.

words.etymology: ラテン語 extrahere。ex-「外へ」+ trahere「引く」。
words.example: The dentist had to extract two of his wisdom teeth.

words.etymology: ラテン語 impartire。in-+pars「部分」。
words.example: The old teacher tried to impart his wisdom to the younger staff.

words.meaning: 徐々に理解される、しみ込む
words.etymology: sink(古英語 sincan「沈む」)+ in。
words.example: It took a few days for the bad news to sink in.

words.meaning: 外に出す、(秘密などを)漏らす、(声を)発する
words.etymology: let「許す」+ out。
words.example: She let out a scream when she saw the spider.

words.etymology: go「行く」+ under。
words.example: Many small shops went under during the economic downturn.

words.etymology: live「生活する」+ off。
words.example: He lived off his savings for almost a year after losing his job.

words.meaning: 合計する、つじつまが合う
words.etymology: add「加える」+ up。
words.example: His story just doesn't add up; something is missing.

words.meaning: 〜を深読みする、〜に別の意味を見出す
words.etymology: read「読む」+ into。
words.example: Don't read too much into his silence; he's probably just tired.

words.meaning: 離陸する、急成長する、脱ぐ
words.etymology: take「取る」+ off。
words.example: Sales took off after the product was featured on TV.

words.meaning: 仲たがいする、抜け落ちる
words.etymology: fall「落ちる」+ out。
words.example: The two old friends fell out over a business disagreement.

words.meaning: こっそり立ち去る、過ぎ去る
words.etymology: slip「滑る、こっそり動く」+ away。
words.example: He slipped away from the party without saying goodbye.

words.meaning: 引き裂く、(契約などを)破棄する
words.etymology: tear「引き裂く」+ up。
words.example: She tore up the letter without reading it.

words.meaning: 中途退学する、脱落する
words.etymology: drop「落ちる」+ out。
words.example: He dropped out of college to start his own business.

words.meaning: 追跡調査する、フォローアップする
words.etymology: follow「従う」+ up。
words.example: The doctor asked me to follow up with a blood test in a month.

words.meaning: 〜を糧にする、〜を食べて生きる
words.etymology: feed「食べさせる、食べる」+ off。
words.example: The rumor fed off people's fear and spread quickly.

words.meaning: 燃え尽きる、疲れ果てる
words.etymology: burn「燃える」+ out。
words.example: She felt completely burnt out after months of overtime work.

words.meaning: (計画などが)だめになる、失敗に終わる
words.etymology: fall「落ちる」+ through。
words.example: Our vacation plans fell through when the flight was canceled.

words.meaning: 食い尽くす、(時間・お金などを)大量に消費する
words.etymology: eat「食べる」+ up。
words.example: The long commute ate up two hours of his day.
